Overwatering kills more houseplants than anything else. Roots need oxygen, and soil that stays wet suffocates them until they rot, turn brown and mushy, and smell bad. The plant then wilts even though the soil is wet, which tricks people into watering more. Check moisture with a finger or a wooden skewer before watering, use pots with drainage holes, and water less in winter when growth slows. A rotting plant can be saved by cutting off dead roots and repotting into fresh [[Potting mix for aroids]].
